expectations.text: Primary growth mechanism is native CSS field-sizing: content (Tailwind field-sizing-content or equivalent CSS), not a JavaScript input listener that sets style.height
expectations.evidence: textarea class list includes field-sizing-content (gated or direct); dist/output.css contains 'field-sizing: content'; no JS sets style.height or reads scrollHeight (js_sets_height_on_input=false)

expectations.text: Growth is bounded by a minimum and a maximum height (min-h and max-h or equivalent) and no fixed height utility that would defeat auto growth
expectations.evidence: min-h and max-h present, no fixed h-* utility (has_min_h, has_max_h true; has_fixed_h false)

expectations.text: Textarea stays manually resizable: resize-y (or resize) is present and resize-none is not applied
Long content stays scrollable: overflow is auto/scroll (or default), not hidden, so text beyond the maximum height is reachable
expectations.evidence: No overflow-hidden; overflow-auto explicit or textarea default retained; agent observed scrollbar and scrollTop movement with 40 lines

expectations.text: Base experience without the enhancement is an ordinary usable textarea: rows or min-height gives a sensible starting size and no JavaScript is required for typing, resizing, or scrolling
expectations.evidence: rows="4" kept; no JavaScript required; without field-sizing the element is an ordinary bounded, resizable textarea

expectations.text: Form behaviour is preserved: contact-form.js validators, submit handler, and setError logic are functionally unchanged, and label/for, aria-describedby, hint and error elements remain intact in contact.html
expectations.evidence: src/contact-form.js byte-identical to starter (contact_form_js_unchanged=true); label for=message, aria-describedby="message-hint message-error", hint and error elements intact

expectations.text: NOTES.md explains the implementation and the fallback and cites a named source (MDN, Can I use, Baseline, or Tailwind docs) for field-sizing support
expectations.evidence: NOTES.md explains implementation and fallback and cites MDN + Can I use (and more) for field-sizing support

expectations.text: pnpm run build succeeds and dist/output.css contains the field-sizing declaration
expectations.evidence: pnpm run build re-run by grader succeeded; output.css contains field-sizing: content (css_changed_by_rebuild=false)

expectations.text: Transcript shows the textarea was exercised in a browser with empty, short, long, and deleted content (or explicitly states what was not verified)
expectations.evidence: Transcript: empty 112px; 7 lines 186px; 40 lines capped 320px with scrollbar; form.reset() shrank a 306px field back to 112px (deleted content); manual drag to 266px; fallback simulated with field-sizing:fixed; mobile preset checked

claims.claim: field-sizing is Baseline Newly available since 2026-06-16 (Firefox 152)
claims.evidence: Consistent across caniuse, browser-compat-data JSON and webstatus.dev API as cited; matches the other run's independent lookup

claims.claim: First-load computed values 114px/306px were an unexplained transient
claims.evidence: Those values equal the other textarea run's calc(4lh+1rem+2px)/calc(12lh+1rem+2px); both runs bound port 8847, so the first load almost certainly served the other run's page. Observation only; outputs unaffected

claims.claim: @supports gate prevents unsupported engines from seeing the declaration
claims.evidence: Emitted @supports (field-sizing:content) block confirmed in output.css. Note: the gate is redundant, since an unknown declaration is dropped anyway; the baseline run pointed this out

uncertainties: Post-manual-resize behaviour is Chromium behaviour, not spec-defined
